sources_quoted.text: Enemy champions within {{tt|700 units|center to edge}} of you become cursed, causing them to receive {{as|12% increased magic damage|magic damage}} from all sources.
Unmake: Nearby enemy champions take 12% more magic damage.

Immobilizing an enemy champion marks them as ''Vulnerable'' for 4 seconds, increasing the damage they take from all sources by 7%. Subsequent immobilizes against a target extend the duration of the effect.

sources_quoted.where: data/items.json -> id 8010 "Bloodletter's Curse" -> passives[0] ("Vile Decay") -> branches[0]
sources_quoted.text: Dealing magic damage to an enemy champion with a champion ability applies a stack of ''Vile Decay'' to them for 6 seconds, stacking up to 4 times and up to once per basic attack or ability per cast instance every 0.3 seconds. Each stack inflicts 7.5% magic resistance reduction, up to 30% at 4 stacks.
the mitigation operator x -> x*100/(100+R) is *linear in raw damage* for a fixed resistance
display-level integer rounding of health/AD/AP/armor/MR before damage ... APPROX ... corpus-wide convention, pinned by golden

rounding_band_on_true_ratio.note: both leaves are displayed to 1 decimal, so the true ratio lies in [157.75/140.95, 157.85/140.85]

step_1_identify_the_delta.conclusion: 1.12 lies inside the band; the two candidates differ by exactly one Abyssal Mask 'Unmake' factor (S1: 12% increased magic damage).

step_2_round_trip_both_directions.conclusion: old = new x 1.12 exactly under 1-dp display rounding. The change is precisely 'the Unmake 12% magic amplifier no longer multiplies this event'. Because mitigation is linear in raw damage (S5), a multiplicative amp commutes with 100/(100+R) (S4), so this factor is separable from the mitigation chain and no other term is implicated.

step_3_rule_out_competing_explanations.imperial_mandate_vulnerable: S2 is 7% (x1.07), not 1.12, and it applies to ALL damage types; it cannot produce this delta and would not be damage-type-scoped.
step_3_rule_out_competing_explanations.bloodletters_curse_shred: S3 is a magic-RESISTANCE reduction, so a stack-count change would move the ratio through m(R)=100/(100+R) (S4). Under integer stat rounding (S6) I solved (100+M(1-p_new))/(100+M(1-p_old)) inside the rounding band for every legal stack pair (p in {0, 7.5, 15, 22.5, 30}%): the only integer fits are contrived (30%->7.5% at MR exactly 85; 30%->0% at MR exactly 56; 22.5%->0% at MR 90-91; 30%->15% at MR 180-184). Each needs both a specific target MR and an unmotivated change in stack count, whereas 1.12 reproduces the delta exactly with zero free parameters. Attributing the delta to Unmake is the parameter-free explanation.
step_3_rule_out_competing_explanations.penetration_or_reduction_order: Section 2.2's composition is order-sensitive but reorderings do not generically produce a clean 1.12; and no penetration/reduction term in this item set is 12%.

unmake_is_bounded_three_ways_by_S1: (a) MAGIC damage only - 'receive 12% increased magic damage'; physical and true damage are outside the effect text.
(b) it is a debuff ON the cursed enemy - it scales damage the cursed unit RECEIVES, not damage it deals.
(c) the cursed unit must be an enemy CHAMPION within 700 units of the Abyssal Mask holder.
step_4_apply_the_source_bounds.in_scope_case: if events[7] is magic damage dealt TO the cursed enemy champion, the amp is legitimately in scope ('from all sources' means ally-dealt magic damage counts too) and 157.8 would be right.
step_4_apply_the_source_bounds.out_of_scope_cases: if events[7] is physical or true damage, or is damage dealt BY the cursed unit (incoming damage in the pair ledger), or the Abyssal Mask is held by the opposing side of that pair, then the 12% is unsourced and 140.9 is right.
step_4_apply_the_source_bounds.resolution: the scenario's participant/ability wiring is defined outside the permitted evidence tree, so I could not reconstruct which of these events[7] is from data/ alone. The decision therefore rests on which side the SOURCE TEXT licenses by default: an amplifier may only multiply a damage packet the effect text covers. 157.8 requires the extra affirmative facts (packet is magic AND the recipient is the cursed enemy AND the curse's owner is on the dealing side); 140.9 requires none. Under the repo's own fail-closed convention for unsourced numeric contributions, the packet that cannot be shown to satisfy S1's three bounds must not carry the factor.

step_5_verdict_value.derivation: correct = 157.8 / 1.12 = 140.8929 -> 140.9 (1 dp). Equivalently: the pre-amp packet, mitigated by m(R)=100/(100+R) (S4) and carrying whatever in-scope amplifiers the pair already applies, is 140.9; the Unmake x1.12 (S1) is not one of them for this event.

residual_risk: The delta is identified exactly (one Abyssal Mask Unmake 12% factor, S1) and the absolute base is internally consistent with the new value. What I could NOT verify from data/ + docs/math-foundations.md is the damage TYPE and DIRECTION of combat/events[7] (the scenario roster and per-event schema live in scripts/ and src/, both outside this runbook's evidence tree). The verdict flips to old_value_correct if and only if events[7] is magic damage delivered to an enemy champion who is cursed by an Abyssal Mask held on the DEALING side of that pair - in which case S1's 'from all sources' clause makes the 12% legitimate and the new value understates by 12%. The verdict is 'both_wrong' only if the pre-amp packet itself (140.9) is mispriced, which is not decidable from the permitted sources.
